STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of mixed leafy greens (looks like arugula/rocket and lettuce with red-stemmed leaves) with a few black olives and a small pale item (possibly a nut or cheese piece). Photographed from above at a steep angle; the white plate is slightly skewed.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White rectangular/trapezoid plate, roughly 30 cm across its longest edge at this angle, so treat it as a ~24 cm side-to-large plate. Vessel area ≈ 3.14 x (12)^2 ≈ 450 cm² (rough, given the non-circular shape).

STEP 3 - Items: mixed leafy greens (arugula/lettuce), 3 black olives, one small pale piece (nut or cheese fragment).

STEP 4 - Area: greens ~10% of vessel (≈45 cm²), olives ~1% (≈4 cm²), pale piece ~0.5% (≈2 cm²). Total food ≈ 11.5% of plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: greens 45 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 135 ml (loose pile); olives 3 x ~2 cm³ ≈ 6 ml; pale piece ≈ 2 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: greens 135 ml x 0.15 ≈ 20 g; olives 6 ml x 0.9 ≈ 5 g; pale piece ≈ 2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: leafy greens ~25 kcal/100 g → 5 kcal; olives ~115 kcal/100 g → 6 kcal; nut/cheese piece assumed ~500 kcal/100 g → 10 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small handful of greens with three olives and a bit of nut/cheese at roughly 27 g and about 21 kcal is plausible for a small side salad. Dressing is not visibly present.
